solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Characters returned from enchanted mountain

indicators.note: characters are letters, so the answer is a run of letters lifted straight out of the next word
something returned goes back the way it came, so the run of letters is read right to left

blocks.note: the middle stretch of the word enchanted

explanation.surface: A wizard's magic mountain gives up a few of its characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' here means letters, not people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a famous peak.

clue.text: Cleric’s waggish academic keeping company

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a dean is a senior university academic

explanation.surface: A churchman described as a playful scholar who keeps up his social life.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman ranking below a bishop.

clue.text: Hopes for area neighbouring Western Isles

blocks.note: aits are small islands in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: A traveller longs for the region next to the Western Isles, the Hebrides off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western Isles' reads as the Scottish island chain but splits into two pieces; an ait (or eyot) is a river islet.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to look forward to it, expecting or wishing that it will come.

clue.text: Financial product one thing to have faith in

blocks.note: a unit is a single item
to trust is to believe in someone

explanation.surface: A sales pitch: this investment is the one thing you can believe in.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled investment fund sold in units to savers, a British form of mutual fund.

clue.text: Muslim kind restraining very destructive deity

indicators.note: restraining something means holding it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: Shia is one of the two main branches of Islam

explanation.surface: A tolerant Muslim holds back someone who is very destructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muslim kind' looks like a gentle believer but means a kind, or branch, of Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is the Hindu god known as the Destroyer within the trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu.

clue.text: Armoured fish finally out to break bones

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the next word only
breaking into something means getting inside it, so a letter goes into the middle

blocks.note: Bones is slang for a doctor, here a surgeon

explanation.surface: A fish with tough plating finally gets out, enough to break your bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' is a slang nickname for a doctor, as in Star Trek's ship's surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon carry rows of bony plates called scutes along the body, a natural kind of armour.

clue.text: Deck cleaner was injured close to pub

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A sailor mopping the deck got hurt near the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop used on ships to wash the decks, and also the sailor who uses it.

clue.text: Arrange song about extraterrestrial orreries?

blocks.note: to plan is to arrange in advance
ET is the standard abbreviation, after the film alien
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Compose a song about a space alien.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is about the alien, so the alien comes first and the song follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system, much like a planetarium; the question mark flags the loose match.

clue.text: With ten howler monkeys around, about to capitulate?

indicators.note: to monkey around is to mess about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Surrounded by ten howler monkeys, a person is ready to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howler monkeys' looks like one animal, but 'monkeys around' is the signal; 'to' does double duty as fodder and as the infinitive of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from boxing, where a cornerman throws a towel into the ring to concede the bout.

clue.text: Sceptic is entertained by Mad Hatter endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter
mad means crazed, so the letters are scrambled out of order
a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A doubter gets invited to the Mad Hatter's endless tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' reads as the Alice character, but 'Mad' is the scramble signal. Here 'is' is both a word of fodder and part of the container phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist doubts or rejects belief in any god, the ultimate religious sceptic.

clue.text: Carefully examining wingless bird

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two outer letters, so both ends are clipped off

explanation.surface: Someone closely inspects a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingless bird' looks like one phrase, but 'wingless' works on the wordplay and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small garden songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: At first they were all nervy — finally showing pluck

indicators.note: at first points at the opening letter of each word that follows
finally points at the closing letter of the next word only

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Everyone was jittery at the start, but in the end they showed courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage, the sense the surface wants, but it is the guitar-string verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the sound of a plucked string, and to twang a string is to pluck it.

clue.text: Feminist writer dressing as biker

indicators.note: dressing someone wraps clothes round them, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch

explanation.surface: A famous feminist author dresses up as a motorcyclist.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist writer of The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Greaser was slang for a leather-jacketed motorcycle youth with slicked-back hair.

clue.text: Strait in Donegal almost gets stormy

indicators.note: almost all means one short, so the last letter is dropped
a storm tosses everything about, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: The weather in the Irish county of Donegal nearly turns to storms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Gate is the narrow channel linking San Francisco Bay to the Pacific, spanned by its famous bridge.

clue.text: Spain stole Brit’s last vessel

indicators.note: last points at the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
a boa is a long feathery scarf, a kind of stole

explanation.surface: Spain made off with a British ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal but is the noun, a wrap worn round the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German torpedo boat of the Second World War.

clue.text: Those prone, possibly near to collapse

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters can be reordered

explanation.surface: People lying flat may be about to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer pinned against the ring's cords is close to defeat, hence the idiom for being about to fail.

clue.text: Suppressed old woman in southeast died

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: old woman is informal slang for one's mother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman in the south-east of England passed away quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something such as a yawn or the truth is to hold it back or stifle it.

clue.text: Elusive creature left knight among radge Scots horsemen

indicators.note: radge is Scots and Geordie slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight vanished among some wild Scottish riders, a creature never pinned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots word 'radge' fits the Highland scene and is the signal; 'among' only joins the pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie, the legendary beast said to live in a Highland lake, has never been reliably sighted or caught.

clue.text: NZ Rail in evil nonsense about going north

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means travelling upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Something wicked and absurd on the railways of New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NZ Rail' looks like a train company, but a rail is a family of wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Notornis is the genus of the takahe, a flightless New Zealand bird in the rail family.

clue.text: Service in French is for German artist

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the Royal Navy, the senior service

explanation.surface: A church service in French is laid on for a visiting German painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship but means one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Modify by blending a paint

blocks.note: to temper is to moderate something by mixing in another ingredient

explanation.surface: An instruction for adjusting a colour by mixing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk, used for early panel pictures.

clue.text: Bar one, wise men understood larval form

indicators.note: bar means except, so a numeral-looking letter standing for one is removed

blocks.note: the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity
got means understood, as in I got the joke

explanation.surface: Every wise man except one grasped the nature of an insect's early stage.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I, the Roman numeral, which is what leaves the wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the soft legless grub of a fly, its larval stage.

clue.text: Drive round with zero speed

blocks.note: O looks like the figure zero
miles per hour, a unit of speed

explanation.surface: Driving in circles at a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' reads as steering a car, but it is the noun for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour or energetic enthusiasm, the same as drive in a person.

clue.text: Saw an early machine gun

blocks.note: first meaning: an old saying or proverb
second meaning: the gun invented by Hiram ... in 1884

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense of see or a cutting tool; here it is an old proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short pithy saying, and the Maxim gun was the first fully automatic machine gun.

clue.text: Live wire securing pole killed person

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: a goer is an energetic, lively person

explanation.surface: An electrified cable fastened to a post has electrocuted someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live wire' paints an electric cable; it means a dynamic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is informal for someone who is dead or doomed beyond saving.

clue.text: Creator of dynamite book coming out for Xmas

indicators.note: something coming out leaves, so that letter is removed from the name

explanation.surface: The dynamite inventor publishes a book just in time for Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book coming out' sounds like publication; it means the B leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a traditional word for Christmas, from the French for the festival.

clue.text: Explosive snores around midnight capture attention

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters land in a new order
around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: read as mid-night: the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: Thunderous snoring in the middle of the night grabs everyone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb someone's whole interest and hold their focus completely.

clue.text: Hellish river flows no more from mouth?

indicators.note: words from the mouth are spoken, so the spelling follows what is said

blocks.note: something that sticks stops moving freely

explanation.surface: A river that has stopped running at its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like a river's mouth, fitting the surface, but signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river bounding the underworld, Hades.

clue.text: Poem in article with wonderful humour

explanation.surface: A review praises a funny piece of verse in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Divine Comedy is the great medieval Italian epic about a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise.
